purpose: Paired genuine Bazel 9.3.0 vs native bazel-rs capture of N17a+b: toolchain_type/toolchain analysis, registered toolchains (register_toolchains, --extra_toolchains), toolchain resolution against the target platform and the host execution platform, platform_common.ToolchainInfo and ctx.toolchains (docs/TOOLCHAINS.md). A<n>: every step of the 11 CLI tests in tests/toolchains.rs (BASE, module texts, BUILD/.bzl texts and expected strings extracted from the test source by artifacts/rustlit.py; native checks replicate the tests' assertions incl. the (CONFIG) normalization); U/: updated rows of tests/common_rule_attributes.rs (exec_compatible_with row), tests/configuration.rs (gap_order_and_select_branch_inputs, whole test), tests/load_declarations.rs (exercised_declarations_fail_explicitly_at_analysis) and tests/native_rules.rs (rules_go_toolchain_targets_analyze, build_wildcards_skip_manual_targets_but_query_lists_them); B<n>/: probes of the design test plan / docs claims. Each chain shares one workspace per side and runs its steps in order. Evidence only; not a BUILD input of any test.

reference.command_flags: --registry=file://<private copy of tests/fixtures/builtin_modules/registry> --repository_disable_download --incompatible_autoload_externally= --lockfile_mode=off --noshow_progress --color=no --curses=no --repository_cache=<private> --distdir=<private: platforms-1.0.0.tar.gz sha256 3384eb1c30762704fbe38e440204e114154086c8fc8a8c2e3e28441028c019a8 + seeded archives>
reference.step_flags: scenario flags then targets (Bazel always has its built-in modules, so bazel_tools/rules_* toolchain registrations are part of every reference resolution)

native.binary: target/debug/bazel-rs (up to date: `direnv exec . cargo build --locked --offline` was a no-op)
native.argv: timeout --kill-after=5 <120|60> bazel-rs --ignore_all_rc_files --cache-dir=private-cache <cmd> [profile args] <flags> <targets> (like the Rust tests)

profiles.plain: no profile args (all A, U and B1-B5 chains, like the tests)

script.harness_origin: /tmp/opencode/bazel-parity-platforms/artifacts/n16c-capture.py (flags, private roots, registry stubs, distdir seeding, env -i, shutdown, scratch cleanup, normalization incl. 7-hex configuration ids, verdicts)

environment: env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin LANG=C.UTF-8 LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 HOME/TMPDIR private, umask 022; scratch under /tmp/opencode removed=True
normalization: messages: `ERROR: <path>:L:C: ` (Bazel) and `bazel-rs: <path>:L:C: ` (native) prefixes stripped (locations compared separately), 7-hex configuration identifiers ('While resolving toolchains for target L (ID)', 'config: ID') replaced by <ID> (raw ids kept in *_config_ids); workspace / output base paths replaced by <<WS>> / <OB>. Native test checks use the tests' own WS / (CONFIG) normalization.

verdicts.EXACT: both succeed; query stdout or the multiset of written output bytes identical (and rule warnings equal)
verdicts.EXACT_MESSAGE: both fail; Bazel's primary message (normalized) ends a line of native stderr (ref_specific_messages_all_in_native: every non-generic Bazel ERROR body too)
verdicts.EXPECTED_NATIVE_UNSUPPORTED: Bazel succeeds; native fails explicitly (not implemented / not analyzed / unsupported option / this module profile does not provide / automatic exec groups / configuration transition)
verdicts.MISMATCH: exit class differs, outputs differ, or both fail and the Bazel message is absent from native stderr (both strings recorded); mismatch_kind sub-classes: starlark_traceback_form (same final Starlark error text), cycle_drawing_omitted, build_file_event_omitted, reference_builtin_registrations / exit_class_reference_builtin_registrations (Bazel fails in rules_java registrations), native_explicit_gap, native_builtin_registrations_not_materialized, exit_class_native_module_resolution, cli_report_source_only_outputs, message, value, exit_class

(were rejected) with Bazel's ignored-directory warning; ctx.toolchains string keys parsed with the innermost calling .bzl (was the rule-defining .bzl: B5/s2_rel failed and B5/s2_app silently built); :* / :all-targets registrations fail explicitly (Bazel crashes); rule(toolchains) with an unknown apparent repository deferred to resolution (B4/unknown_repo, query_unknown_repo); the BUILD-file event also for a missing type in the rule's own package; no blank line after an empty missing_toolchain_error; registration pattern texts ('no targets found beneath', 'while parsing', 'Analysis of target L failed; build aborted: No repository visible', 'Expected absolute target patterns'); the RegisteredToolchains cycle drawing and Bazel's choice of the last cycling registration; dir(ctx.toolchains) == ['toolchain_types'] and toolchain_types(); ToolchainInfo() positional-argument text; Starlark provider-requirement text; Bazel's label-syntax message for string keys. Tests: A6 strict_u / strict_o removed from tests/toolchains.rs (genuine Bazel fails on rules_java's registrations; kept as B2 probes strict_u / strict_o); tests A8 (whole_repository_registration_patterns), A9 (registration_pattern_errors_and_toolchain_cycles) and A10 (string_keys_use_the_calling_bzl_and_starlark_api_details) added with their mirrors; capture check 'stderr_contains' added.
run_history.implementation and test changes between: ctx.toolchains string keys: the marker/rerun mechanism (rerun of the implementation per string-keyed access, up to 4096 times, fallback to the rule-defining .bzl) is replaced by a vendored-interpreter hook: StarlarkValue::at_with_location / is_in_with_location (defaults delegate to at / is_in) called by the ArrayIndex and In bytecode instructions with the expression's lazily computed span; the module of that span is the calling .bzl (inlined helpers keep their own spans); no location or a non-label module name fails explicitly. Escaped ctx.toolchains values (stored in providers) are indexed with the downstream caller's .bzl, and their ToolchainInfo files are provider files. Test A11 (escaped_toolchain_contexts_and_many_string_keys) added with its mirror.

observations.negative_extra_toolchains: --extra_toolchains=-//tc:other_any: Bazel accepts and builds //u:o with name=other (consistent with a negative pattern only subtracting from patterns listed before it; the --extra_toolchains come first); native fails explicitly (documented).
observations.reference_crash_star_patterns: --extra_toolchains=//names:* and //names:all-targets (B1, A9/extra_tc*) crash genuine Bazel 9.3 (exit 37, NullPointerException in FilteringPolicies$RuleTypeFilter.shouldRetain: file targets have no rule); since run 4 native fails explicitly ('toolchain registration pattern ... is not implemented in the native profile: Bazel 9.3 crashes expanding it ...', docs/TOOLCHAINS.md).
observations.check_toolchain_types_host_platform: Genuine Bazel registers the built-in modules' toolchains; rules_java's have target_settings targets (@@rules_java++toolchains+*//:version_or_prefix_version_setting, @@rules_java++toolchains+local_jdk//:local_jdk_settings_alias) that themselves resolve toolchains. With a check_toolchain_types host platform as the only execution platform they fail with 'Unable to find an execution platform for target platform P from available execution platforms [P]' (+ 'Analysis failed' at the consumer), so every toolchain-using build fails in Bazel. The native plain profile has no such registrations; the allowed_toolchain_types behaviour once asserted by the test (//u:u builds, //u:o 'No matching toolchains') is not reproducible with genuine Bazel, so run 4 removed those steps from tests/toolchains.rs (B2 probes strict_u / strict_o keep the evidence; unit tests cover allowed_toolchain_types). Which rules_java target is reported varies between runs.
observations.builtin_profile (B6): With --experimental-builtin-modules native analyzes every built-in registration (D1) and fails offline at '//tools/test:all' (@@rules_shell+ not materialized); rules without toolchain types (genrule, plain Starlark rule) and direct toolchain targets build on both sides. Without the built-in profile (--registry only) toolchain resolution with an explicit --host_platform/--platforms is EXACT, and the default host platform fails explicitly natively while Bazel resolves (@platforms//host: //u:o builds, //u:u 'No matching toolchains').
observations.selection_order: Root before dependencies, --extra_toolchains reversed/last wins with duplicates keeping the last copy, :all by name, /... subpackages first, dependency dev registrations ignored, root dev registrations interleaved in order and dropped by --ignore_dev_dependency, manual toolchains kept, filegroups filtered from :all, explicit non-toolchain labels rejected: all EXACT / EXACT_MESSAGE (A2, B1).
observations.constraints_and_settings: libc-style default (toolchain constrained to gnu.2.28 rejected by a platform with the default; explicit "unconstrained" matches the default), exec-side defaults, use_target_platform_constraints both ways, duplicate constraints (also the same label twice), target_settings with config_setting, alias, select() alias (config_setting_group shape), flag_values, unrelated broken toolchains failing every toolchain-using rule while rules without types still build: all EXACT / EXACT_MESSAGE (A3, A4, B2, B3).

def _probe_impl(ctx):
    t = ctx.toolchains
    by_label = t[Label("//tc:type")]
    by_string = t["//tc:type"]
    relative = t[":type_alias"]
    lines = [
        "type=" + type(t),
        "repr=" + repr(t),
        "label=" + by_label.name,
        "same=%r" % (by_label == by_string and by_string == relative),
        "info_type=" + type(by_label),
        "info_dir=%r" % dir(by_label),
        "tool=" + by_label.tool.basename,
        "optional=%r" % t["//tc:other_type_missing"],
        "optional_in=%r" % ("//tc:other_type_missing" in t),
        "actual_in=%r" % ("//tc:type" in t),
        "undeclared_in=%r" % ("//tc:other" in t),
        "alias_impl=" + t["//s:alias_impl_type"].name,
    ]
    out = ctx.actions.declare_file(ctx.label.name + ".txt")
    ctx.actions.write(out, "\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    return [DefaultInfo(files = depset([out]))]

def _show_impl(ctx):
    out = ctx.actions.declare_file(ctx.label.name + ".txt")
    lines = []
    for name in ["mode", "flags", "count", "env", "strip", "stamp", "debug", "dep"]:
        value = getattr(ctx.attr, name)
        if name == "dep":
            value = str(value.label) if value else None
        lines.append(name + "=" + repr(value))
    lines.append("files=" + repr([f.short_path for f in ctx.files.srcs]))
    lines.append("conditions=" + repr([str(t.label) for t in ctx.attr._config_dependencies]))
    ctx.actions.write(out, "\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    return [DefaultInfo(files = depset([out]))]

    "dep": attr.label(allow_files = True),

})

With a check_toolchain_types host platform as the only execution platform they fail with 'Unable to find an execution platform for target platform P from available execution platforms [P]' (+ 'Analysis failed' at the consumer), so every toolchain-using build fails in Bazel. The native plain profile has no such registrations; the allowed_toolchain_types behaviour once asserted by the test (//u:u builds, //u:o 'No matching toolchains') is not reproducible with genuine Bazel, so run 4 removed those steps from tests/toolchains.rs (B2 probes strict_u / strict_o keep the evidence; unit tests cover allowed_toolchain_types). Which rules_java target is reported varies between runs.
